title: Social Security Numbers exposed in the NDH bulk export
headline: No Social Security Numbers remain in the 2026-10-07 NDH bulk export. The dashed-SSN pattern matches zero of 7,481,907 Practitioner and zero Organization resources, against 46 confirmed exposures in 2026-04-09 and 41 in 2026-05-08. CMS has now removed them rather than partially scrubbing them. The scan is unchanged and still reads the same fields: 7,451,577 of those Practitioner resources still carry the qualification array the exposures were found in, so the zero is an empty result and not an empty query.
notes:
Re-runs the scan that independently verified the 2026-04-30 Washington Post finding, against the 2026-10-07 NDH bulk export (loaded into BigQuery as `cms_npd.practitioner`/`cms_npd.organization`), matching the dashed SSN format \\d{3}-\\d{2}-\\d{4} in the full resource JSON. It finds no confirmed exposures in either resource type. Earlier releases carried 46 (2026-04-09) and 41 (2026-05-08), most of them in qualification.identifier.value, the state-license slot. The zero is checked, not assumed: 7,451,577 of 7,481,907 Practitioner resources still carry the qualification array those exposures were found in, so the scan is reading the right field. Privacy posture is unchanged: AINPI publishes counts, JSON locations, NPIs (professional IDs, not PII) and state breakdowns, never SSN values.

Release watch, Practitioner.birthDate: 0 of 7,481,907 Practitioner resources carry birthDate (0 year only, 0 more precise than the year). The positive control is gender, read in the same scan: 7,481,907 carry it, so a zero here is an empty field and not an empty query. The HL7 NDH STU2 draft adds a warning-severity invariant that birthDate carry only the year (Jira FHIR-57885); the published STU1 (https://hl7.org/fhir/us/ndh/STU1/) has no such constraint. AINPI publishes counts only, never the dates.

definitions.full_date: birthDate is longer than four characters (YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD)
